builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
summary: It replaces iterative diffusion or flow-matching sampling for probabilistic time-series forecasting with Koopman-patch latent extrapolation, a closed-form matrix-exponential single-step generator, and an adaptive per-variable/per-horizon uncertainty gate. The cost is added model and implementation complexity, dependence on learning a stable Koopman latent representation, and likely retraining or integration work rather than drop-in use on an existing forecasting stack. It can fail if the learned linear latent dynamics poorly approximate strongly nonlinear or regime-switching series, if the closed-form generation becomes unstable over longer horizons, or if the reported gains do not transfer from benchmark data to the reader's workload.
rationale: The method is directly relevant to constrained production inference because it targets forecast quality and sampling latency without requiring foundation-model scale, but its benefits need validation on the reader's own time-series distribution and horizon requirements.
technique: Koopman latent operator for single-step probabilistic time-series forecasting

The cost is added model and implementation complexity, dependence on learning a stable Koopman latent representation, and likely retraining or integration work rather than drop-in use on an existing forecasting stack. It can fail if the learned linear latent dynamics poorly approximate strongly nonlinear or regime-switching series, if the closed-form generation becomes unstable over longer horizons, or if the reported gains do not transfer from benchmark data to the reader's workload.
At least 25x reduction in inference time compared with iterative generative forecasting models, while reporting SOTA accuracy on 13/17 CRPS and 16/17 NMAE ProbTS benchmarks.
